variants.name: Live signal: JCI, rupiah, INDOGB 10Y trend, INDOGB–UST spread
US 10Y trend in place of the INDOGB trend
Korea-style rotation (JCI inverted: stocks down = bonds up)

ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

src: Yahoo Finance: IDX Composite (^JKSE) and USD/IDR (IDR=X) daily closes; any USD/IDR close more than 1.5% from Bank Indonesia’s JISDOR fix is replaced by JISDOR. INDOGB 10Y: PHEI IGSYC (CNBC benchmark 10Y before the first stored PHEI day). US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: USD/IDR 4-week % change (inverted: a weaker rupiah is bond-bearish)
INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 26-week average (wide = cheap)

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); spread vs its 130-day average; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 130-day average (wide = cheap)

notes.headline: Vice President Gibran resigns: the JCI jumps 2.7% with foreign buying, but the rupiah sets a record low at JISDOR 18,241 and the 10Y INDOGB edges up to 7.69%; the daily signal improves to −0.67 and a new sell-off episode, opened Nov 10, is flat so far. Signal −0.67: bond sell-off
notes.now: Stocks and the rupiah split today: the JCI rose 2.66% to 5,250.90 after Vice President Gibran resigned and MSCI's November review came in as expected, with foreigners net buying Rp443.5bn across the market, yet the rupiah fell 0.48% to a record-weak JISDOR of 18,241 as the dollar rallied on December Fed-hike pricing. Over 20 sessions the JCI is still down 12.62% and USD/IDR up 1.70%, so the month-long picture remains one of foreign money leaving Indonesian stocks; in bonds, Bloomberg-compiled data show $174m of foreign inflows so far in November, though who traded today is not published. The daily signal rose to −0.67 from −0.77: the JCI part eased to z −1.29, while the 10Y trend part (z +1.82, the 10Y up 51.9bp over 20 sessions) and the rupiah part (z +0.57) stay bearish, and the spread part is the one bond-bullish input (z +1.01). INDOGBs pay 271bp over Treasuries, 27.3bp above the 130-day average and in the 92nd percentile of 52 weeks; that is a nominal pick-up before currency risk. Treasuries explain little of the trend: over four weeks the INDOGB 10Y is up 50.9bp while the US 10Y fell 12bp, and with a 26-week weekly beta of −0.22 only +2.7bp is the Treasury-linked part and +48.2bp is residual, which is what the US move does not explain rather than proof of domestic selling or political risk. There was no New York cash session overnight (Veterans Day), so Treasuries explain none of today's +1.6bp at the 1-year daily beta of 0.33; Tuesday's 10bp US jump implied about +3.3bp that INDOGBs have not priced, and cash Treasuries reopened about 2bp higher, so some catch-up risk remains. On the daily build the Oct 7 episode ended Nov 6 with the 10Y 51.0bp higher, and a new sell-off episode opened Nov 10 and is +0.5bp after three sessions. Since June 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 0.74 outright and 0.87 hedged against Treasuries, but sell-off calls were right only 51% of the time over the next 20 sessions (rally calls 58%), and the average 10Y move after a sell-off call was −1.8bp; these are in-sample back-tests. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: neutral on duration rather than short, because sell-off calls have had little edge and both auction and foreign bond demand are holding up; the rupiah and BI's Nov 17–18 decision are now the main risk to the front end.
notes.flip: The daily signal is in sell-off below −0.5 and sits at −0.67. A return to neutral needs the 10Y trend to cool as the mid-October jump rolls out of the 20-session window, plus a JCI holding above 5,200 with the rupiah back near 18,050. A deeper sell-off would come from JISDOR moving further past its 18,241 record, a JCI relapse below 4,900 or the 10Y above its 7.72% high. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers are a BI-Rate hike that steadies the rupiah (bearish for the front end on the day, bullish for the trend after) or MSCI softening its Standalone proposal; an orderly MPR choice of a new Vice President would remove the political trigger, a drawn-out one would sharpen it.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.

JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link; on the weekly build the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024), while the daily build did better over the same span.
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and now weighs more. JCI −42% from its peak to about 5,251, 10Y up to 7.69%: the second and deeper foreign exit, though foreigners bid Rp18tn at the Nov 10 auction and Bloomberg-compiled data show bond inflows in November. Vice President Gibran resigned on Nov 12: stocks rallied, but the rupiah hit a record low and the daily signal stayed in sell-off (−0.67).
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money, and any statement about who bought or sold is a hypothesis. USD/IDR is Yahoo's close, replaced by Bank Indonesia's JISDOR fix on any day it strays more than 1.5% (Yahoo printed ~17,480 from Nov 3, 2026 while JISDOR was ~18,100); the 20-session windows count stored sessions, so gaps in the data stretch them. Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The daily back-test runs from June 2022 (959 sessions): the live signal makes 190bp outright (Sharpe 0.74) and 216bp hedged against Treasuries (Sharpe 0.87), against −39bp for always holding the 10Y; the weekly build scores 0.42 and 0.57. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score up to 0.73 outright and 0.78 hedged on the weekly build but were picked after the fact and are not live. In-sample, no trading costs; not a trading system.
